historical_summaries: extended-heuristic-training, 2 runs, Jul 18–19 2026 — dead end: Early heuristic-heavy training was highly asymmetric and extension did not repair the weak side.
all-heuristic-curriculum, 2 runs, Jul 20 2026 — dead end: Substantially greater/all-heuristic exposure was a dead end in both variants.

reproduction-and-forgetting, 3 runs, Jul 20–21 2026 — finding: The original short regimen reproduced strong mean performance, while snapshot continuation sharply forgot offensive-first play; a fresh longer schedule largely recovered the mean but retained a zero worst side.

potential-reward-shaping, 6 runs, Jul 21–24 2026 — finding: Unshaped training produced the best controlled terminal mean; shaping strength and defensive weighting failed to improve the weakest matchup.
warmup-duration-control, 2 runs, Jul 24 2026 — finding: The nominal longer reproduction strongly beat the shortened warmup, rejecting the idea that shortening warmup was harmless.
combined-heuristic-shaping, 3 runs, Jul 26–27 2026 — dead end: Combined-only heuristic training remained brittle; removing shaping modestly improved mean, while defense-biased shaping did not.
full-combined-defense-weight, 4 runs, Jul 28–31 2026 — finding: At full duration, defense weight 1.5 was the useful shaping setting; weight 2 raised mean slightly but reduced worst-side robustness.

defensive-opening-curriculum, 4 runs, Aug 1–3 2026 — dead end: The initial opening-curriculum variants did not consistently improve robustness; the no-opening annealed/shaped variant had the best mean in this group.
fixed-defensive-curriculum-shaping, 2 runs, Aug 3 2026 — finding: After the curriculum fix, slight shaping improved the pair but absolute robustness remained low.
center-mask-shaping-and-lr, 3 runs, Aug 4 2026 — finding: Annealed learning rate plus slight shaping was a meaningful recovery over both center-masked controls.

mistake-rate-block-reward-interaction, 6 runs, Aug 4–6 2026 — finding: Without block reward, starting mistake rate 0.7/0.5 beat 0.3; adding block reward 0.5 collapsed performance despite high collected block reward.
block-reward-coefficient-sweep, 3 runs, Aug 7 2026 — finding: The controlled sweep located a moderate optimum at 0.25; 0.4 collapsed and 0.1 was intermediate.
long-block25-refinements, 3 runs, Aug 8 2026 — finding: At 0.25 and 15.36M steps, slight shaping hurt while opening probability 0.4 modestly improved the mean.

block20-opening-retries, 4 runs, Aug 16–17 2026 — finding: Reducing block reward to 0.20 improved long-run robustness, and opening probability 0.4 slightly raised mean but slightly lowered worst side in completed retries.

current_findings.finding: Full heuristic-only warmup with block reward 0.15 produced the strongest robust model; lower/higher nearby coefficients and mixture schedules did not surpass it.

scope.chronology_basis: MLflow meta.yaml start_time; run-name dates are not assumed reliable

global_caveats: All terminal evaluations use finite games per side and most variants have one seed, so close differences can be sampling noise.

Six status-1 runs—df624486aa56409d8f50269333723a28, f9c8f998888648a0ba59c78757125476, 0c572fdacc98462798966e1aad118c63, a6eb2d709e8e4adfba0ee5f4deb9be06, 1f9a5292b74e47ada012c9ba6a8e7246, and 099be2bb21fb48bc83980bc2ef6cb38a—are incomplete and are never treated as terminal rankings.
Metric schemas evolved: early runs omit episode lengths and some aggregates, so absence is not interpreted as zero.
Cross-group chronology often changes multiple parameters, curriculum implementations, or loaded snapshots; causal claims are restricted to close within-group controls.

patterns.name: Mean performance is a poor proxy for robustness
patterns.interpretation: The highest mean run is side-specialized; the later warmup run sacrifices mean but raises the weakest of six policy/side cells ninefold.

patterns.name: Block reward has a non-monotonic optimum and proxy-reward risk
patterns.interpretation: Collecting more shaped block reward is negatively associated with game strength at high coefficients; moderate 0.15-0.25 settings are promising, with 0.15 strongest in the later full-warmup regimen.

patterns.name: Potential shaping is context-sensitive and usually negative
patterns.interpretation: Shaping hurt in clean/near-clean comparisons more often than it helped; the corrected-curriculum improvement coincided with a learning-rate change.

patterns.name: Defense weight 1.5 is better than slight unbiased shaping, but does not solve side brittleness
patterns.interpretation: Weight 1.5 gives the best robustness of this controlled sequence; weight 2 chases mean at the expense of the weakest cell.

patterns.name: Defensive openings help modestly only after the core regimen is sound
patterns.interpretation: Probability 0.4 repeatedly adds 0.02-0.045 mean but slightly lowers worst-side rate; it is a mean/robustness tradeoff, not a breakthrough.

patterns.name: Annealed learning rate can rescue shaped center-mask training
patterns.interpretation: This is one of the cleaner schedule comparisons, but it needs seed replication and worst-side logging interpretation.

patterns.name: Longer or continued training can forget rather than monotonically improve
patterns.interpretation: Snapshot-pool continuation requires checkpoint selection and anti-forgetting evaluation rather than assuming terminal improvement.

champion.selection_criterion: Best completed-run per-policy/per-side robustness: maximize eval/worst_win_rate first, then require competitive eval/average_win_rate and inspect all six policy/side win rates with paired episode lengths. This avoids selecting a high-mean model that collapses on one side.

other_strong_comparator.reason: Similar mean but materially weaker combined-policy O-side robustness.

why_not_highest_mean.reason: Its larger mean is driven by extreme matchup/side specialization; its weakest cell is nine times lower than the champion's 0.18.

evaluation_requirements: Primary metric: eval/worst_win_rate over every logged heuristic/side cell.
Secondary metric: eval/average_win_rate; report every component win rate rather than aggregate alone.
Pair each per-policy/side win rate with its *_avg_episode_length where logged.
Use replicated seeds and confidence intervals before promoting small terminal differences.
Never rank status-1 partial runs against completed terminal results; use them only as trajectory evidence.

prioritized.direction: Replicate and locally tune the champion's block reward around 0.15 under the exact 15.36M heuristic-only warmup regimen.
prioritized.hypothesis: Coefficients near 0.15 preserve the champion's 0.18 worst-side robustness better than 0.10 or 0.20 while retaining mean strength.
prioritized.design: Run multiple seeds at 0.10, 0.125, 0.15, 0.175, and 0.20 with every other champion parameter fixed; predeclare eval/worst_win_rate as primary and average_win_rate as secondary.
prioritized.caveat: The 0.10 run belongs to attempt 2 and the 0.20 run to attempt 1; exact replication is required before assigning coefficient causality.

prioritized.direction: Optimize directly for the champion's weakest Combined-policy O side without sacrificing its other five cells.
prioritized.hypothesis: A small curriculum reweighting toward combined-policy O-side situations can lift the current 0.18 floor while preserving defensive/offensive strengths.
prioritized.design: Start from the champion, change one opponent/opening mixture knob at a time, and gate checkpoints on the minimum of the six win rates; always log paired episode lengths.
prioritized.caveat: Episode length is descriptive and direction-dependent; longer games are not automatically better without win-rate improvement.

prioritized.direction: Test annealed learning rate on the champion regimen as a clean one-knob experiment.
prioritized.hypothesis: Annealing 0.0003 to 0.0001 may stabilize late warmup competence and reduce side collapse.
prioritized.design: Compare fixed and annealed schedules across seeds with champion reward/curriculum settings unchanged and evaluate checkpoints, not only terminal models.
prioritized.caveat: Evidence is currently one center-mask pair and does not establish transfer to the champion curriculum.

prioritized.direction: Use defensive-opening probability as a constrained mean/robustness tradeoff rather than maximizing it.
prioritized.hypothesis: A value between 0.30 and 0.40 may retain the 0.30 setting's worst-side rate while capturing part of the 0.40 setting's mean gain.
prioritized.design: Sweep 0.30, 0.325, 0.35, 0.375, 0.40 around an otherwise fixed champion configuration with replicated seeds.
prioritized.caveat: The observed mean gains are small and unreplicated.

prioritized.direction: Add anti-forgetting checkpoint selection before any self-play continuation.
prioritized.hypothesis: Selecting on the minimum per-policy/side checkpoint and maintaining heuristic rehearsal will prevent the continuation regressions seen after snapshot loading.
prioritized.design: Evaluate every snapshot on all policy/side cells, retain Pareto-optimal checkpoints, and compare continuation with versus without fixed heuristic rehearsal.
prioritized.caveat: Existing continuation runs also changed schedules, so the mechanism needs a controlled test.

prioritized.direction: Avoid high block-reward and broad all-heuristic regimens unless redesigned with explicit robustness guards.
prioritized.hypothesis: High proxy reward and indiscriminate heuristic exposure divert learning from winning behavior.
prioritized.design: Treat block_reward_coef >=0.4 and all-heuristic schedules as negative controls; if revisited, monitor train/mean_block_reward jointly with each policy/side win rate and stop on proxy divergence.
prioritized.caveat: These are regimen-level dead ends; they do not prove every alternative implementation of broad heuristic exposure will fail.
